divergence: What if Antikythera-style mechanisms had scaled into industry?

branches.title: Geared Tides Guide Ocean Sailors
branches.summary: Rhodes workshops produce portable geared calculators that predict tides, lunar phases, and star positions for long sea voyages. Scaling the Antikythera gear trains into standardized brass instruments makes reliable open-ocean navigation possible centuries earlier.
branches.scene: At dawn, a captain cranks a palm-sized brass cosmos while its pointers sweep over a painted Aegean chart.
branches.reviewNote: Direct portable use of original astronomical gearing; Rhodes workshops and timing highly plausible.

branches.title: Mechanical Heavens Enchant Public Theaters
branches.summary: Athenian artisans scale celestial gearwork into room-sized planetariums and self-moving mythological automata for festivals and schools. Because the original mechanisms already encoded planetary cycles in bronze, enlarging them turns calculation into immersive public art and astronomy education.
branches.scene: Children gasp as a bronze Helios drives his chariot around a domed ceiling, overtaking a silver moon on geared tracks.
branches.reviewNote: Scaling celestial gears into automata is direct, though post-sack Athens weakens timing.

branches.title: Clockwork Pumps Green The Delta
branches.summary: Alexandrine engineers link waterwheels to Antikythera-style gearboxes driving Archimedes screws and timed sluices across the Nile Delta. Precise ratios from astronomical mechanisms allow reliable low-lift irrigation, expanding farms and wetlands far beyond annual floodplains.
branches.scene: Rows of clicking wooden gear towers lift glittering ribbons of Nile water into lotus-lined canals at sunset.
branches.reviewNote: Industrial gear transfer plausible, but power pumps need torque, not astronomical precision.

hero.imagePrompt: Photorealistic dawn scene on an ancient Greek ship departing Rhodes, centered on one large brass orrery resting on a wooden table in sharp focus in the foreground, its interlocking gears, circular engraved dials and sweeping pointers clearly visible as a captain's hands turn its small crank over a painted Aegean chart, with softly blurred sailors, mast, rigging and calm Aegean sea in golden morning light behind it, historically authentic details and no modern elements.
